subject: CrestlineAI renewal — pilot benchmark & scale contingency
messages:
From: Eric Tan <eric.tan@crestline.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: maya.s@crestline.ai, procure@crestline.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + pilot request — benchmarking for scale

Hi Dylan,

Quick context: our contract with Redwood is up in March. We're committed to staying long-term if we can validate throughput and tail-latency at three production load profiles (20k, 60k, 120k tokens/min) and confirm the Dedicated path before Q2. Our infra team also has a parallel pilot with BlueMantle for a potential replatform.

Can Redwood run a short, focused pilot that demonstrates:
- sustained 120k tok/min for 30m without >200ms p95 gen latency
- KV cache hit characteristics for our prompt templates
- quantized-16 performance and memory profile on an n1-standard-40 equivalent instance

We want a concise results packet for procurement and our CTO by 2/8. I'm attaching a short ask doc. If you can sketch a timeline and what committed capacity you'd need from us (reserved vs burst), that will help our internal procurement conversation.

Attachments: [crestline-request-20270121.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks — Eric
Eric Tan
Head of ML Platform, CrestlineAI
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Eric Tan <eric.tan@crestline.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + pilot request — benchmarking for scale

Eric — thanks for the brief. We're aligned on the ask. Looping in Marissa (AE) and Rishi (solutions) to propose a concrete benchmark plan; Naomi from CS for rollout/runbook and SLO alignment. High-level notes:

- We can run a 5-day focused pilot combining Dedicated pool slices + transient burst lanes to simulate steady-state and spike behavior.
- We typically validate p95 generation and end-to-end tail via our tracing hooks; Rishi will propose a schedule and what we'll need from your side (sample prompts, keys, and small traffic driver).
- If Crestline is prepared to commit to a 12-month reserved uplift (X GPUs committed), we can put a firm latency SLA + a one-time onboarding credit to accelerate; details once we have numbers.

Marissa — any constraints from pricing/approval side if they sign a 12-month uplift of dedicated capacity?

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, Eric Tan <eric.tan@crestline.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + pilot request — benchmarking for scale

Eric / team — drafted a proposed benchmark plan, timeline, and minimum inputs below. See attached plan and an initial results snapshot from an internal dry-run using a model variant close to yours.

Plan (5 business days):
Day 0: ingest sample prompt corpus + confirm sequence length distributions (we need 3k examples covering templates).
Day 1: warm KV cache and run steady-state 20k tok/min profile for 1 hour; capture p50/p95/p99 + GPU util and mem.
Day 2: ramp to 60k tok/min with mixed prompt-size distribution; enable prefix caching.
Day 3: sustained 120k tok/min for 30 minutes; run separately with quant-16 path and float32 baseline.
Day 4: failure modes & rollback — simulate node loss and confirm automatic routing to compatible variants. Finish with a short runbook + results packet.

Minimum inputs from Crestline:
- sample prompt corpus (3k items)
- representative model artifact (or model name + config)
- a sandbox API key and traffic driver VM for load shaping

Notes from internal dry-run (initial-results-snapshot.csv attached):
- quant-16 showed ~2.4x throughput vs fp32 with ~18% delta in some hallucination-style QA tests (we'll surface quality metrics).
- p95 during 120k runs hovered ~180ms for token Gen; end-to-end p95 (including network) was ~230ms with our probe harness.

Attachments: [benchmark-plan-crestline.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), initial-results-snapshot.csv (text/csv)]

I'll own the test harness and can start as soon as we get the corpus + sandbox key. Happy to do a short sync tomorrow.

—Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Eric Tan <eric.tan@crestline.ai>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 24 Jan 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + pilot request — benchmarking for scale

Team — short fiscal note for leadership: if Crestline commits to a 12-month dedicated uplift (estimate: 8x A100-equivalent reserved units) we can offer the following commercial package to be reviewed by revenue ops:
- 18% committed discount on per-token pricing for reserved capacity (applies to baseline throughput up to committed units)
- One-off onboarding credit equal to 4 weeks of reserved fees to offset pilot costs
- 90-day SLA for latency (p95 targets) with an operational playbook and penalty cap (needs legal review)

I recommend we hold the discount on the condition they: sign SOW within 30 days of pilot completion, and agree to a mutually scoping appendix that defines benchmark pass criteria (p95 under X ms, mem, and quality deltas under Y%). If we fail the benchmark, they'll get scaled credits rather than termination rights.

I'll draft a short commercial summary + SOW skeleton (SOW-draft-v1.pdf) and route through RevOps for a fast-track. If anyone expects pushback on the numbers, flag now.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOW-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

4) 2/9–2/28: If SOW signed, onboarding + pilot-to-prod ramp; schedule a canary in production week. (Owner: CS + Eng)

Outstanding asks from our side:
